1. The works, and the designs, and the purposes of God cannot be
    frustrated, neither can they come to naught.

The works, and the designs, and the purposes of God cannot be frustrated, neither can they come to nought: for God doth not walk in crooked paths ; neither doth He turn to the right hand nor to the left ; neither doth He vary from that which He hath said ; therefore His paths are straight, and His course is one eternal round.

2. Remember, remember, that it is not the work of God that is frustrated, but the work of men: for although a man may have many revelations, and have power to do many mighty works, yet, if he boasts in his own strength, and sets at nought the counsels of God, and follows after the dictates of his own will, and carnal desires, he must fall and incur the vengeance of a just God upon him.
